main_body: Palm-like tree: a star-shaped frond crown (rows 0-17) on a tall thin brown trunk (rows 18-54)
top_band: light green (L~142, #71a854) rows 2-6 at x=16, closed by a dark outline row 7, then darker fronds (L~55 down to ~28)
evidence: The crown reads as fronds splaying outward, with a lit top patch (rows 2-6, L 142) clearly stepped from the darker fronds below (L 55 to 28). A dark outline row 7 acts as the front edge, and the very dark rows 11-17 under the crown act as its shadow. The trunk is a vertical south face with ring banding. There are no receding side faces. Borderline, since the top is a small patch, but the crown is not a flat elevation.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 13 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile, against roughly 108 per tile and 427-567 colours in the references. The crown has about 5 green steps, but they are blocky and have no leaf clumps. The trunk is just two alternating browns in a striped pattern, so it is very thin next to the textured, root-flared reference trunks. The dark outlines are partly tinted (16% neutral) and look like a dark green/brown sticker edge. Overall it is far flatter and sparser than the Beodeul trees.
